extracted.intended_audience: federal agency accountants, auditors, financial statement preparers and users (PTO, Department of Commerce, OMB, GAO)
extracted.subtask_description: Notes and accounting-policy guidance for preparing and presenting the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (PTO) consolidated financial statements (fiscal year 1999), including recognition, measurement, classification, and disclosure requirements. Intended to guide PTO preparers, auditors, and oversight bodies on treatment of revenue, assets, liabilities, expenses, leases, actuarial liabilities, and related budgetary accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions are recorded on the accrual basis of accounting as well as on a budgetary basis. Under the accrual method, revenue is recognized when earned and expenses are recognized when goods or services are received; the accompanying financial statements are presented on the accrual basis of accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgetary accounting enables compliance with the requirements for and controls over the use of Federal funds. Record transactions both on accrual (for financial statement recognition) and budgetary bases (for legal/appropriation control).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of Federal Accounting Principles (GAAP/SFFAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The accounting principles and standards applied are in accordance with GAAP for the Federal government and the following hierarchy: (1) Individual standards agreed to by the Director of the OMB, the Comptroller General, and the Secretary of the Treasury and published by the OMB and the General Accounting Office; (2) Interpretations related to the SFFASs issued by the OMB in accordance with OMB Circular A-134; (3) Requirements contained in the OMB's Form and Content Bulletin in effect for the period covered by the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting principles published by other authoritative standard-setting bodies and other authoritative sources may be applied (a) in the absence of other guidance in the first three parts of the hierarchy, and (b) if their use improves the meaningfulness of the financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Accounting and Fee-Funded Status
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO has been fully fee-funded since FY1993; budgetary accounting is used to enable compliance with Federal fund use requirements and controls. Certain fee revenues are offsetting collections subject to annual congressional limitation and are available until expended; funds authorized but not used are carried forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of PTO's fee-funded structure and statutory revenue-withholding (OBRA), withheld revenue constitutes offsetting receipts deposited in a restricted special fund at Treasury and may be used only as authorized by Congress and as made available by a Treasury warrant. Excess moneys not appropriated are retained in the restricted receipt account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and Classification of Revenue (Exchange, Deferred, Customer Deposits)
rubrics_metrics.description: User fees remitted with initial applications and requests for services are recorded as exchange revenue when received, with an adjustment at year-end to defer revenue for services not yet performed. Amounts remitted for services not yet requested are recorded as liabilities in customer deposit accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue withheld pursuant to OBRA is also recognized as exchange revenue. Application fees that have undergone initial processing but not yet reviewed by examiners/attorneys are deferred and recognized to the extent costs are incurred in the initial processing phase. Issue fees are earned over an eight-week processing cycle and recognized to the extent costs are incurred; remaining amounts are unearned. Undeposited checks are treated as cash equivalents but may lead to deferred revenue classification when services have not been performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity vs Non-Entity Asset Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Assets an entity is authorized to use in its operations are entity assets; assets held by an entity but not available for the entity's use are non-entity assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for a portion of the Fund Balance with Treasury, all of the PTO's assets are entity assets and are available to carry out the PTO mission within budget constraints. Customer deposit accounts are non-entity until an order is placed and funds are reclassified to entity funds once ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund Balance with Treasury — Classification and Control
rubrics_metrics.description: All banking activity is conducted per Financial Management Service directives; amounts of unrestricted funds held by Treasury available to pay current liabilities are limited each year by Congress in the PTO's annual appropriation; all disbursements processed by Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund Balance is presented by unrestricted and restricted funds (appropriated, unobligated, revenue withheld) and by entity and non-entity subtotals. Customer deposit accounts are non-entity funds until reclassified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization Policy for Property and Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization thresholds: for individual purchases ADP equipment, software, software in progress, furniture, equipment = $25,000 or greater; for bulk purchases thresholds vary (e.g., $500,000). Contractor costs for developing custom software are capitalized when incurred for design, coding, and testing; software in progress is not amortized until placed in service; all other property and equipment acquisitions are expensed upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully depreciated assets purchased prior to October 1, 1996 may be written off against accumulated depreciation. Buildings are leased from GSA and considered operating leases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation Methods and Service Lives by Asset Class
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation is primarily straight-line (SL) with specified service lives: ADP equipment 3–7 years, software 3–11 years, furniture 5 years, equipment 3–5 years. Software in progress is not depreciated until placed in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide acquisition value, accumulated depreciation, and net book value by class in disclosures. Depreciation expense is included in program/operating expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Advances and Prepayments
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO prepays amounts in anticipation of future benefits; although payment has been made, an expense is not recorded until goods have been received or services performed. Advances to personnel for travel are recorded and expensed after travel has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain deposit accounts (e.g., with Government Printing Office and DOC) to facilitate recurring transactions. Disclose remaining prepaid amounts and expected time to expend (example: NIHF prepayment expected to be expended by March 31, 2000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postemployment Compensation and Related Liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for on-the-job injuries fall under FECA administered by DOL; DOL bills agencies annually as claims are paid but payment deferred two years for budgetary funding. PTO records liabilities for claims paid on its behalf during benefit periods. Unemployment insurance claims billed quarterly; accrual and disclosure of liabilities are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual leave and compensatory time are accrued as earned and adjusted each fiscal year to reflect current pay rates; sick leave and non-vested leave are expensed as taken. If current/prior funding is not available to pay for earned but unused leave, funding will be obtained from future financing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of Employee Retirement Systems and Benefits (Imputed Financing)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO employees participate in CSRS or FERS; the PTO's financial statements do not report CSRS or FERS assets or accumulated plan benefits — reporting is OPM's responsibility. The PTO recognizes an imputed financing source and corresponding expense representing the PTO's share of the cost to the Federal government of providing pension and post-retirement benefits to eligible employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the amounts of PTO contributions for CSRS and FERS participants and amounts contributed to Social Security (FICA). Describe thrift savings plan contributions (mandatory 1% plus matching 1–4% for FERS participants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and Classification of Liabilities; Coverage by Budgetary Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO records as liabilities all amounts likely to be paid as the direct result of events that have already occurred. Liabilities are considered covered by: (1) realized budgetary resources, (2) unrealized budgetary resources, and (3) cash and Fund Balance with Treasury. Unrealized budgetary resources are collections in excess of amounts appropriated for current fiscal year spending that become available later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts covered vs not covered by budgetary resources and explain reasons (e.g., withheld fees in restricted special fund are not considered resources until appropriated; the fee structure with low initial application fees supplemented by maintenance fees requires additional budgetary resources to cover unearned revenue). Provide tables showing liabilities covered and not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred Revenue — Types and Measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred revenue represents fees received for requested services not yet fully earned. Two types recorded: (1) checks received with a request for service not yet deposited due to lag time, and (2) fees for applications partially processed or collected issue fees for patents not yet issued. Application fees processed initially but not reviewed are deferred and recognized to extent of costs incurred; issue fees earned over an eight-week processing cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report deferred revenue by program (patents, trademarks, information dissemination) and by component (unearned fees, undeposited checks). Provide reconciliation of total deferred revenue amounts as of fiscal year end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial Liability Estimation for FECA (FWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: FECA future workers compensation liability is estimated by DOL using actuarial procedures developed for FECA benefits; estimates include expected liability for death, disability, medical and miscellaneous costs for approved compensation cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projected annual benefit payments are discounted to present value using OMB economic assumptions for ten-year Treasury notes and bonds. Disclose interest rate assumptions used for discounting and the resulting estimated liability amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease Classification and Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating lease agreements negotiated by GSA for PTO office buildings are considered operating leases. Rent expense is recognized and future minimum lease payments are disclosed by fiscal year for the commitment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose total rent expense for fiscal years and provide schedule of minimum lease payments for future years through the committed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed Financing Source and Expense Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO recognizes an imputed financing source and corresponding expense to represent its share of the cost to the Federal government of providing pension and post-retirement health and life insurance benefits (Pension/ORB) to eligible employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose components (CSRS/FERS, FEHB, FEGLI) and amounts for each fiscal year in the required supplemental information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Presentation of Program/Operating Expenses and Allocation Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Program or operating expenses consist of costs directly charged to business activities and costs allocated to business activities. Allocated costs are distinguished between those centrally managed for efficiency but directly controllable within activity management and indirect charges controlled at a PTO-wide level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate allocated costs between directly allocated and indirect; present total program/operating expenses by expense category (personal services, contractual services, depreciation, etc.) and by responsibility segment (Patents, Trademarks, Intellectual Property Policy, Information Dissemination). Provide tables of direct, allocated, and allocated indirect expenses and subtotals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to Budgetary Resources — Components and Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to budgetary resources include available recoveries, unavailable collections and recoveries, rescission of prior year funds, and the resulting total adjustments to resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present components and totals of adjustments to budgetary resources for the fiscal year and comparative prior year amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments and Contingencies — Disclosure and Estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose obligations for undelivered orders (purchase orders placed but goods/services not yet received) and reasonably possible contingent liabilities from routine administrative proceedings, legal actions, and claims (including ranges where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide amounts for undelivered orders and unpaid amounts; when litigation/claims are reasonably possible, disclose estimated ranges (example: reasonably possible labor relations claims $750 thousand to $7,500 thousand) and discuss Judgment Fund treatment for certain tort/contract settlements that may be paid by other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intragovernmental Assets and Liabilities Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Required supplemental information discloses intragovernmental assets (Fund Balance with Treasury, accounts receivable, prepayments) and intragovernmental liabilities by agency (e.g., Department of Commerce, Treasury, OPM, GPO) and by category (accounts payable, accrued payroll, postemployment compensation, customer deposit accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables showing agency-level balances for intragovernmental receivables, prepayments, accounts payable, accrued payroll and benefits, accrued postemployment compensation, customer deposit accounts, etc., to enable reconciliation with consolidated balances.
